issues.item: Triggers: Loss Themes: Talk about people loosing loved ones
issues.explanation: The loss-themed trigger is hard to reconcile with the indexed trauma of physical abuse by a romantic partner. It implies bereavement-related activation, but there are no corresponding memory, threat, or appraisal items about death, losing a loved one, or grief. In this profile it stands out as clinically mismatched rather than merely unusual.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Authority Figures: Being around people in authority or uniform
issues.explanation: Avoiding authority figures or uniforms is not well linked to the reported trauma type or the rest of the profile. For intimate-partner physical abuse, this strategy would need supporting material suggesting the perpetrator was an authority figure or that uniforms became trauma cues, but no such trigger, threat, memory, or appraisal items are present. It therefore looks disconnected from the formulation and symptom pattern.

vignette: Meet Kai, a 63-year-old widowed construction worker from Oceania. He's been struggling to cope with the memories of physical abuse he suffered at the hands of his late wife. The trauma has left an indelible mark on his life, and it's only recently that he's begun to realize the extent of its impact. It started when Kai would see specific body parts – a wrist, a shoulder – that reminded him of the way his wife used to grab or push him during their arguments. These visual triggers would transport him back to those moments, making him feel like he was reliving the abuse all over again. As he recalls, "I'd be working on a site, and I'd see a guy with a similar build to my wife's, and suddenly I'm right back there, feeling helpless." Talking about the event or being around people related to it would also set him off, making him feel like he was losing control. To cope with these feelings, Kai developed some maladaptive strategies. He started carrying large amounts of cash on him at all times, impulsively spending money on things he didn't need just to distract himself from the memories. "It's silly, I know," he says, "but when I'm feeling anxious or scared, buying something new makes me feel like I've got some control back." He also became obsessed with staying near exits whenever he was in a room or building, always scanning for potential escape routes. This habit even extended to his construction work, where he'd position himself near the site's entrance just in case. But these strategies didn't alleviate Kai's sense of threat; if anything, they seemed to heighten it. He started waking up multiple times during the night to check whether he was safe, and ordinary sounds would make him jump or startle. "I'll be lying there, and suddenly I'll hear a creak or a groan, and I'm convinced someone's breaking in," he admits. This constant state of hypervigilance left him feeling drained and on edge. As Kai struggled to manage these symptoms, his negative appraisals began to solidify. He started believing that he was weak, that he couldn't rely on himself to get through tough situations. "I keep thinking about all the times I didn't stand up for myself during those arguments," he says, shaking his head. "It's like I'm reliving my own failure over and over." This emotional numbness has also left him feeling disconnected from the world around him – like he's just going through the motions. Kai's maladaptive strategies only seemed to reinforce these negative appraisals. His compulsive spending, for example, made him feel guilty and ashamed, further solidifying his sense of weakness. And when he avoided conflict or confrontation, it only confirmed to himself that he was indeed unable to rely on himself. Despite the exhausting cycle of triggers, maladaptive strategies, and negative appraisals, Kai is finally seeking help. The recent loss of a close friend has left him feeling isolated and alone, and he's begun to realize that his coping mechanisms are no longer sustainable. "I just want to feel like myself again," he says, looking down at his hands. "I don't know if I can ever go back to who I was before all this happened, but I have to try."
